Title: Sword-wielding man leaves two injured in Gua Musang
Article:
GUA MUSANG: Two men were injured after being slashed with a sword during a fight at a rubber store at Rancangan Pemulihan Tanah (RPT) Kesedar Sungai Terah yesterday.
The incident, which occurred at 8.30pm, was believed to have stemmed from a dispute over the disposal of broken mosaic tiles and damage to a closed-circuit television (CCTV) camera at the store.
Gua Musang police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred during a discussion where a 27-year-old man allegedly tried to pull out a sword tucked behind his back.
"One of the victims tried to stop him, leading to a struggle. The suspect then swung the sword.
"As a result, the first victim, 33, suffered an 18cm cut to his left cheek, while the second victim, 40, sustained a 5cm cut to his right arm," he said when contacted.
He said one of the injured men was still receiving treatment at a hospital.
Sik said the suspect tried to flee after the incident but was detained by members of the public before being handed over to police.
"Police also seized a sword with a wooden sheath and a knife to assist investigations.
"The case is being investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt with a dangerous weapon," he said.

Title: Hong Kong arrests 9 over fuel smuggling as oil prices surge
Article:
HONG KONG: Hong Kong arrested nine people in a city-wide operation targeting illicit fuel activities, authorities said on Wednesday, as surging global oil prices continue to put pressure on the import-dependent financial hub.
The city lacks its own refineries and imports its entire supply of automotive fuel, with much of it coming from neighbouring mainland China.
Prices at Hong Kong's filling stations are among the world's most expensive, creating a growing incentive for smugglers to transport cheaper fuel illegally across the border into the city.
Authorities said they seized more than 30,000 litres of smuggled fuel worth more than HK$1 million (US$127,000) in September, arresting eight men and one woman.
Criminals are using modified cross-boundary trucks or private cars with enlarged fuel tanks to smuggle fuel through control points, Chong Sin-han, a senior investigator at the customs department, told reporters on Wednesday.
"Fuel prices remain persistently high, tempting illegal traders to sell more untaxed gasoline for profit and tempting citizens to take risks by purchasing it," said Chong.
Authorities seized vehicles that "were unventilated, increasing the risk of fire or explosion", said Leung Nam-cheuk, a fire officer at the anti-illicit fuelling activities task force.
The retail price of standard petrol reached about HK$34.60 per litre in Hong Kong this week, which saw a jump of 16.6 per cent since late February as the Middle East conflict disrupts global shipping and strains energy supplies.
Hong Kong also saw rises in freight and insurance costs, which pushed diesel prices to record highs, authorities told lawmakers on Wednesday, noting the Strait of Hormuz shipping routes faced significant disruptions and that Saudi Arabia's oil infrastructure came under renewed attacks.
As of September, Hong Kong customs officials had arrested at least 84 people suspected of engaging in illegal fuel dealings this year and seized 95,000 litres of fuel.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore set to miss 2035 green-power import target
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore is set to fall short of its 2035 target of importing 6 gigawatts of low-carbon electricity, a report from research and consultancy firm Wood Mackenzie said on Wednesday.
The country has approved 9.25 GW of import capacity across six corridors, but none of the projects has reached financial close or begun construction, the report added.
Here are the key points from the report:
Singapore generates up to 95 per cent  of its electricity from natural gas. By 2035, imported green power is likely to be at 15 per cent  of its power generation mix, roughly half of EMA's target of about one-third of projected demand at 6 GW.
Key obstacles include export permit regimes, project bankability, cross-border transmission financing and the lack of a mechanism for buyers to claim the carbon value of imported power.
Malaysia is the only corridor with a credible path to delivery this decade through an existing interconnector with up to 1 GW of capacity.
EMA approved 900 MW of imports from Johor, in August, including 300 MW for Sembcorp Utilities that could begin supplying power by 2029.
Sarawak, which has secured a cable supplier, is realistically targeting commercial operation in the mid-2030s.
Indonesia accounts for 37 per cent  of the approved pipeline, but progress has stalled due to export permit requirements and local-content rules.
Vietnam, Cambodia and Australia together account for 43 per cent  of the pipeline, though all remain at the conditional approval stage with no visible construction timeline.
Imported power must compete with Singapore's wholesale electricity price, while EMA has also expanded plans for hydrogen-ready gas-fired generation.--REUTERS

Title: 'We don't have a future': French students protest school conditions
Article:
As drums pounded and chants rang out, 16-year-old Yanis, flanked by a knot of friends, rattled off why he had joined tens of thousands surging through the streets of Paris on Tuesday to demand better learning conditions.
"There are no toilets, no toilet paper, everything is broken," he said, his schoolmates nodding and chiming in.
"We go to class from 8am to 6pm with a one-hour break."
"There are 36 of us in class. We can't study," the teenager from the northern Paris suburb of Sarcelles said, calling conditions at his high school "unacceptable".
He was among some 56,000 people who poured onto the streets of Paris on Tuesday as part of a protest movement that began in late September.
Across France, students and teachers have blocked entrances to hundreds of high schools for 15- to 17-year-olds, protesting against teacher shortages, overloaded timetables, ill-equipped classrooms and buildings not designed to cope with rising temperatures.
On Tuesday, protesters flooded into the Place de la Republique in central Paris, hoisting signs.
"2026 is the new 1789," declared one, a nod to the French Revolution.
Another placard took the form of an oversized middle finger.
The scent of merguez sausages — a fixture of French demonstrations —drifted through the square.
Demonstrators danced and clapped to pounding drums, breaking into chants calling for President Emmanuel Macron to resign and denouncing the far right ahead of presidential elections next year.
But beneath the festive atmosphere, some of young protesters struck a bleaker note.
Fidele, 15, who had come with Yanis, dreamt of becoming a lawyer, but said conditions at his school had left him pessimistic about whether he could get there.
"When I see the system, I tell myself that I don't have a future" in this country, he said.
Nearby, 16-year-old Noham has his sights set on becoming a computer engineer, but worried that overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages were putting that ambition out of reach.
"Without access to an education, I can't have the job I dream of," he said.
"It's an enormous amount of stress."
Nadine Zilliacus, an educator for 20 years, said she has seen the same disillusionment take hold among even younger pupils, who increasingly express a "really dark" view of what lies ahead.
"We tell them you have to prepare for the future with a job you like," she said.
"Even in middle school, they tell us: 'There's no point anyway. We won't have jobs'."
Further along the route, the crowd pressed towards the march's endpoint, clapping and chanting before voices swelled into a rendition of Marseille, France's national anthem.
From a balcony overhead, a silver-haired woman leaned out to encourage protesters below.
Spotting her, the crowd turned their faces upwards and broke into chants of "Mamie! Mamie!" — an affectionate French term for grandmother.
Among those making their way through the crowd was Ami, 17, who travelled into Paris with a group of friends to protest against conditions at her high school in the city's suburbs.
"Compared with schools in central Paris, we're neglected."
As the march reached the Nation roundabout, the festive mood began to shift, with police carrying riot shields barring the route and some protesters throwing stones at officers.
As Ami and her friends drew closer, the boom of tear gas canisters fired by police cut through the singing. The girls screamed and stopped in their tracks, unsure whether to keep moving forward.
Nearby, a middle-aged woman had mascara streaking down her face after being caught in the tear gas, while a young man comforted her.
Ami said she did not understand the police response.
"We're just protesting, we're singing and that's all," she said, adding that she was scared.
After a day of drums, chants and dancing through the capital, she was ready to leave.
"We just want to go home."
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 713 deepfakes of political leaders taken offline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 713 image-manipulation and deepfake content involving political party leaders have been taken down between Jan 1, 2025 and Sept 15 this year.
The Communications Ministry said the content was taken down following complaints, breaches of service providers' community guidelines and violations of local laws.
"The misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, including deepfakes, scams and identity forgery, is dealt with based on the nature and elements of the offence and the jurisdiction of the relevant ministry or enforcement agency.
"For content containing obscene, indecent, false, threatening, grossly offensive or harmful elements, MCMC may take action under the Communications and Multimedia Act or the Online Safety Act," it said in a written parliamentary reply today.
The ministry was responding to Afnan Hamimi Taib Azamudden (PN-Alor Setar), who asked about the number of complaints and action taken against deepfake content involving political party leaders between 2025 and 2026.
The ministry said MCMC's requests for takedowns were based on the law, the elements of the offence, facts and evidence, regardless of the political affiliation, position or background of those involved.
The ministry said cases involving prosecution were referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers for assessment, while prosecution could only proceed after written consent was obtained from the public prosecutor.
Cases that proceeded to court were subject to the judicial process, with accused persons given the right to mount a defence before a decision was made.
"The ministry also has checks and balances to ensure MCMC acts fairly and independently without external pressure.
"Parties aggrieved by MCMC's actions and decisions may appeal to the Appeal Tribunal established under both Acts before seeking judicial review at the High Court if dissatisfied with the tribunal's decision.
"This mechanism helps ensure MCMC's regulatory and enforcement actions are carried out based on the law, facts and evidence and are subject to the appropriate review process," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mohamad: Early preparations underway for possible extreme El Nino heat
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The government is making early preparations for potentially extreme heat, with temperatures forecast to reach 40°C from the end of this year until April next year.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said his ministry is also seeking input from experts in artificial intelligence, science and technology to identify the best ways to deal with the expected weather changes.
"We are in the midst of looking for solutions, including from experts in AI technology, science and other fields, on how to deal with temperatures reaching 40°C from the end of this year until April next year, as forecast," he said at the "Dinner with Parti Amanah Negara President" event here today.
He said early preparations were important to ensure that the government and the people would not panic in the event of prolonged hot and dry weather.
Mohamad said one issue that needed attention was the possibility of water shortages, which could affect the agriculture sector, including crop cultivation and livestock activities.
He said early information and weather forecasts were also being taken into account to enable appropriate measures to be planned in advance.
Meanwhile, Mohamad hopes the 2027 Budget, to be tabled on Friday, would give attention to his ministry in view of the challenges expected to arise from the El Nino phenomenon.
"I think there may be some additional allocation for the ministry because one of the challenges we will have to face is El Nino next year," he added.
He said the water supply issue also needed to be addressed early to ensure that the country's agriculture sector and food security would not be affected in the event of a prolonged period of hot weather.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sri Lanka's Rajapaksa family hit as ex-first lady arrested in graft probe
Article:
COLOMBO: Sri Lanka's anti-graft authority arrested former first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa on Wednesday over allegations that her charity misused donations collected for a children's hospital, dealing a major blow to the once powerful family.
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake's government has revived long-dormant graft investigations involving members of the once-powerful Rajapaksa family, which dominated Sri Lankan politics for nearly two decades.
The 73-year-old wife of former president Mahinda was remanded in custody until Tuesday by a Colombo magistrate.
She was arrested earlier in the day by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) which questioned her for nearly seven hours.
"The magistrate ordered her to be held in custody till Oct 13 and to admit her to the prison hospital because of an eye condition," a court official told reporters outside the Colombo Magistrate's Court.
In another development, a Rajapaksa-era foreign minister, Rohitha Bogollagama, was also arrested Wednesday for corruption.
The Colombo High Court ordered the 72-year-old Bogollagama to be held in custody till the end of a trial against him for misusing state funds in 2006 when he was minister of investment promotion.
The former first lady was arrested in connection with an investigation into her Siriliya Saviya Foundation, which had raised money to buy equipment for hospitals, including a children's cancer facility.
Her lawyer, Manoj Gamage, told reporters that she denied the allegations made against her and will contest the charges of misappropriating donations raised for charity.
The CIABOC also arrested the former head of a state-owned bank after accusing him of giving 10 million rupees (US$30,000) to her charity, the agency said.
Pradeep Kariyawasam, the then-chairman of the National Savings Bank was released on bail.
- FAMILY UNDER SIEGE -
Shiranthi Rajapaksa travelled to Singapore on Sept 16 for medical treatment, and was served with a summons at Colombo airport to provide a statement to police about her charity.
She flew back on Monday after filing a court petition seeking to prevent her arrest, but the hearing for anticipatory bail was fixed for Oct 12.
Police said the authorities wanted to question Shiranthi Rajapaksa over the donations collected by her charity for a scanner intended for a cancer hospital for children.
Investigators told a court that the scanner had already been donated by the Chinese government, but the charity allegedly continued to solicit donations and misused the funds.
Shiranthi Rajapaksa has denied any wrongdoing, saying the money had not been misappropriated.
Other members of the family have also faced legal troubles.
The former first lady's eldest son, opposition lawmaker Namal Rajapaksa, is in remand custody over allegations linked to a 2013 Airbus aircraft deal signed during his father's presidency.
The Rajapaksa family has consistently denied the corruption allegations and dismissed the cases against them as politically motivated.
Mahinda Rajapaksa served as president from 2005 to 2015 and remains one of Sri Lanka's most influential political figures, despite the decline in the family's fortunes since mass protests ousted his brother, Gotabaya Rajapaksa, from the presidency in 2022.--AFP

Title: The arms race is becoming a debt race
Article:
If you think all the new investment spending pouring into the world economy right now is solely targeted at Big Tech and artificial intelligence, you're only half right.
According to some estimates, the planned increase in Group of Seven (G7) defence spending over the next decade may match it — even if the overlap between the two is now huge.
Another measure of the simultaneous stimulus to global economic activity and inflation — alongside pressure on public purses and rising borrowing rates—is the eye-popping scale of planned defence spending over the coming decade.
Former United States Navy Admiral James Stavridis, now managing director and partner at The Carlyle Group, estimated this week that additional defence commitments from G7 governments over the next 10 years will amount to some US$8 trillion of additional re-armament spending on top of prior trends.
With the collective annual gross domestic product (GDP) now just over US$55 trillion for the US, Japan, Germany, France, Britain, Italy and Canada, an US$8 trillion increase over a decade amounts to almost 15 per cent of 2026's GDP.
Stavridis points out that G7 defence spending has risen to two per cent of GDP, its highest share in more than 30 years, with that share projected to rise to 3.8 per cent as soon as 2030.
Across Europe alone, he said, broader defence goals imply roughly €4 trillion to €5 trillion of additional spending over the coming decade —rising towards €9 trillion "when adjacent infrastructure is included".
The earmarked increase in US defence outlays in the 2027 fiscal year to a record US$1.5 trillion would surpass the World War 2 peak in inflation-adjusted dollars.
According to the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimates, that level of defence spending by then would amount to some 4.6 per cent of the US GDP —just shy of 2009's peaks and approaching levels last seen at the height of the Cold War in the 1980s.
That budget boost may bring the US defence bill back above the current estimate for annual Treasury debt servicing costs — although at the rate at which bond yields are rising, there could be a protracted race between the two to gobble up US tax dollars.
The main point Stavridis makes is that this spending is likely to be very different in terms of procurement than in the past—far less on warships and tanks and more on tech, drones, cybersecurity and battlefield AI.
"The centre of gravity is moving towards smaller, faster-moving companies in cyber, encryption and hypersonics rather than the traditional prime contractors, and the deals being struck are correspondingly smaller and more numerous," he wrote.
Data centres and their security are another common factor between both.
This is nowhere more salient than in Europe, where the Russian threat to Europe's eastern borders, doubts about US commitment to the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation under President Donald Trump and a ratcheting up of defence spending across the continent combine in ways that some hope will also boost its tech sector.
"Two decades of declining European defence investment tracked closely with two decades of declining European tech competitiveness, a pattern the current rearmament cycle appears determined to reverse," Stavridis noted.
All of which will be cold comfort for restive government bond markets having to absorb the additional borrowing that goes with these increases.
The defence-to-debt-servicing ratio has historically been cited as a warning metric signalling debt sustainability concerns.
The Washington-based Institute of International Finance recently estimated that average government borrowing costs across the G7 are now at their highest since mid-2008, while annual interest expenses are nearly 85 per cent higher.
Over the past year, advanced economies paid more than US$ 3.3 trillion in interest on internationally traded government bonds alone —more than the estimated US$2.6 trillion of global spending on AI, US$3.1 trillion on defence or US$2.3 trillion on clean energy.
The sheer scale of economic stimulus from both the defence and AI splurges may be at least reining in debt-to-GDP ratios.
But there's little doubt that the world's major economies are now entering a high-octane, highstakes balancing act that may achieve its goals but risks increasing instability in the process.
No one is fully sure where this all ends.
The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thaksin fights US$504m tax claim, citing threat to personal safety
Article:
BANGKOK: Ex-Thai premier Thaksin Shinawatra told a court on Wednesday that his life could be in danger if authorities seize assets including bullet-proof vehicles as part of a US$500 million, decades-old tax dispute.
The Supreme Court's Tax Division last November upheld a tax claim by the Revenue Department against the former prime minister – one of Thailand's richest people – over the 2006 sale of his telecoms firm.
Thaksin has sought a temporary injunction against the Revenue Department to stop it from seizing his assets to pay the bill, which his lawyer Winyat Chatmontree told AFP was worth more than 17 billion baht (US$504 million).
Appearing at the Central Tax Court in Bangkok on Wednesday, Thaksin said those assets included five cars, two of them bullet-proof, which he linked to his personal safety.
The 77-year-old said he had faced four attempted assassinations while in office. He was elected premier in 2001 and again in 2005, before being ousted by the army in 2006.
"I am not sure if someone intends to harm me," Thaksin said, adding that if his cars were taken, "what if my life is in danger? Who will take responsibility?"
Thaksin also argued that he has already settled the bill for the tax-free sale of Shin Corp to Singapore's Temasek Holdings.
The 2006 deal, which netted the Shinawatra family a US$1.9-billion windfall, sparked protests and became a lightning rod for opposition to Thaksin's populist government.
He was ousted in a coup later that year and went into exile for more than a decade, during which time he was convicted of corruption.
When he returned in 2023, Thaksin was arrested but sent to hospital and then freed. He finally saw the inside of a jail last year, serving eight months before his release in May.
The tax court is due to deliver its ruling on Nov 16.
The Shinawatra clan has for two decades been the key foe of Thailand's pro-military, pro-royalty elite, who view their populist brand of politics as a threat to the traditional social order.
But the Shinawatra dynasty has faced a series of legal and political setbacks, including the court-ordered removal of Thaksin's daughter, Paetongtarn, as prime minister in August 2025 over an ethics breach.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Scam syndicates are evolving, Malaysia must outsmart them
Article:
Receiving suspected scam calls  is almost an everyday event for Malaysians now. News of victims who fell for such scams and in the process lost money in the tens or hundreds of thousands, if not millions, of ringgit have become commonplace as well.
It used to be that unsuspecting Malaysians regularly fell for job offers that were too good to be true in neighbouring countries, only to be forced into the unsavoury task of swindling other people of their cash.
After recent high-profile  crackdowns on such scam operations in places like Cambodia, the perpetrators seem to be on the move. Malaysia is in their sights but it is most reassuring that the authorities are on alert and on the lookout.
Police have just identified a rented villa in rural Melaka where 11 Japanese as well as four Chinese and two Myanmar citizens were arrested and the usual scam operation paraphernalia seized.
The syndicate operating this centre is said to be targeting victims in Japan. And at an abandoned resort in Pahang , the Immigration Department netted 98 people, 95 of whom are foreigners, suspected of being members of another scam-call syndicate.
Scam centres are changing, moving across international borders and trying to blend into out-of-the-way locales in order  to avoid detection. Our crime-busters must, therefore, be quick to stay ahead of these syndicates as well.
The above two raids prove that our enforcement agencies are capable of tracking increasingly sophisticated syndicates. However, one or two busted operations do not mean the problem is under control.
Scam operators are proving highly adaptable, mobile and increasingly technology-enabled. When one location becomes too hot, they move — sometimes across borders, sometimes just a few hours away from the city.
The authorities must  be equally adaptable and need to stay ahead rather than merely respond after the fact. Vigilance must extend beyond traditional hotspots to seemingly quiet, remote and abandoned properties.
Ordinary Malaysians must also be alert and quickly report any suspicious movements and activities in their midst.
These are highly lucrative illegal operations and the operators can be counted on to be highly creative as well in order to avert getting caught.
There is, therefore, no room for complacency and resting on the laurels of a few busted operations.
There must be no let-up in hunting down such operations wherever and whenever they  sprout up. Every dismantled operation should also provide invaluable clues and intelligence to assist in identifying the next one.
Enforcement agencies, local authorities, property owners and the community at large must all remain alert to unusual activity. The syndicates are constantly changing their playbook.
Malaysia needs to do the same to get a step or two ahead of them. A whole-of-society approach is required to tackle this menace.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thailand, US trade deal down to final clause: PM
Article:
SINGAPORE: Thailand is at "the last paragraph" of a trade agreement with the United States, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Wednesday.
Speaking at a forum in Singapore, Anutin said he expected to sign the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade during President Donald Trump's next visit to Asia, likely in November in Manila or Shenzhen when Trump attends Asean meetings.
Anutin said that he received a letter from Trump last week confirming the deal is at its final stage. "He told me that I was to make sure that my people and the United States Trade Representative would write up the final clause."
In July, the US imposed a tariff of 12.5 per cent on imports from Thailand.
The United States is Thailand's largest export market, accounting for 24 per cent of the southeast Asian country's total exports so far this year.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt reviewing SST for elderly care services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Finance and Women, Family and Community Development Ministries are reviewing proposals to improve the Sales and Service Tax (SST) for elderly care services regulated by the Welfare Department.
The Finance Ministry said the review would consider the type and nature of services provided, including basic and premium care, to ensure a more targeted tax treatment.
"The government is aware of concerns over the impact of the service tax on the costs borne by elderly people receiving care services.
"This is especially as demand for these services is increasing in line with the growing number of elderly people in Malaysia as the country becomes an ageing nation," it said in a written parliamentary reply today.
The ministry was responding to Datuk Shahelmey Yahya (BN–Putatan) on whether SST exemptions could be extended to elderly care centres and homes.
It said elderly care services are subject to SST under the Service Tax Regulations 2018, with a registration threshold of RM500,000 that had been in effect since Sept 1, 2018.
It added that the proposed improvements would be announced once finalised, taking into account the views of stakeholders and relevant implementation considerations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nine states record 100pct Sara usage rate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nine states and federal territories to record a 100 per cent usage rate for the monthly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) as of Sept 20.
The Finance Ministry said these were Kedah, Kelantan, Perlis, Sabah, Sarawak, Terengganu, Perak, Pahang and Labuan.
"The lowest usage rates were recorded in Putrajaya at 94 per cent and Johor at 95 per cent.
"Based on data as of Sept 20, nearly 8.4 million monthly Sara recipients under the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah had used their MyKad to purchase basic necessities at registered premises.
"This reflected a usage rate of 99.7 per cent, with transaction value in the local market reaching RM5.2 billion," the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply today.
The ministry was responding to Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman (PN-Sik), who asked about Sara spending by state as of September.
For Sara Untuk Semua, the ministry said more than 20 million Malaysians had made purchases, representing 90 per cent of all recipients, with transaction value in the local market reaching nearly RM1.9 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nurse, husband killed in motorcycle-lorry crash
Article:
PETALING JAYA: A couple were killed in a motorcycle-lorry crash at Jalan Sungai Buloh, near the Sierramas exit today.
Petaling Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said police received a report on the crash at 3.50pm.
"Preliminary investigations found that the crash occurred around 2.50pm.
"The victims lost control of their motorcycle before colliding with a lorry driven by a local man in his 30s," he said in a statement.
He said the male motorcyclist, in his 30s, and his wife were pronounced dead at the scene.
The lorry driver was taken to the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters for further investigation, including for an initial urine screening test.
"The initial urine screening test on the lorry driver was negative. The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act.
"Witnesses who saw or were at the scene are urged to come forward at the nearest police station or contact Traffic Investigation Officer Inspector Maslina Musa at 013-4025834 to assist investigations," he said.
Earlier, several posts of the crash were making rounds on social media.
The female victim was reportedly a nurse at Selayang Hospital.
Selayang Hospital later confirmed in a Facebook post that its Emergency and Trauma Department trained nurse, Noor Athirah Yaacob, died today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-cop, 76, has 12-year jail term, whipping upheld for assaulting girl, 5
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today upheld a retired policeman's 12-year prison sentence and two strokes of the rotan for sexually assaulting a five-year-old girl whom his daughter had been babysitting.
A three-member bench comprising judges Datuk Azman Abdullah, K. Muniandy and Dean Wayne Daly dismissed the 76-year-old man's appeal against his conviction and sentence.
Azman said there was overwhelming and convincing evidence, notwithstanding that the victim was eight years old when she gave evidence.
He said her testimony remained consistent with the contents of the police report lodged by her father and the medical report.
He said the heinous act had not only left the victim with physical injuries but had also caused her deep psychological distress.
"The law exists as a bastion of justice to protect the weak. In this case, the victim is a child who was incapable of resisting or fully comprehending what the appellant did to her," he said.
Azman said the sentence imposed was intended to serve as a reminder not only to the appellant but also to the general public that age does not confer a licence upon any person to act with impunity towards a child.
The court issued a warrant of committal for the man to commence his sentence from today.
The man, who was present in court in a wheelchair, had previously been granted a stay of execution of his sentence and bail of RM10,000 with one surety pending disposal of his appeal, which was heard today.
Azman said the execution of the whipping conviction would be determined by the prison authorities based on whether or not he is fit to undergo the sentence.
Earlier, lawyer Mohd Rusnizam Abdullah told the court that his client had met with an accident and his health had deteriorated.
On April 19, 2024, the Kuantan Sessions Court found the man guilty of sexual assaulting the victim at a house in Kuantan in 2020.
He was sentenced to 12 years' imprisonment and two strokes of the rotan. The High Court upheld the Sessions Court's decision on Jan 27 this year.
At today's proceedings, Mohd Rusnizam argued that the victim was not competent to testify because she did not fully understand the implications of giving truthful evidence and the consequences of lying.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Jasmee Hameeza Jaafar, however, submitted that the victim was a competent witness as she remembered vividly what had happened.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: Finas to study residual payment mechanism for actors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Communications Ministry, through the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas), will study the residual payment or revenue-sharing mechanism for audiovisual works in Malaysia.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the study would take into account three main aspects, namely legislation, the structure of the creative industry ecosystem and current business models, and the practices of streaming platforms and international distributors.
"The study will examine whether the mechanism should be implemented through amendments to existing laws, industry guidelines or standard contracts," he said in a parliamentary written reply today.
He was responding to Kalam Salan (PN-Sabak Bernam) on whether the government planned to introduce a residual payment or rerun royalty mechanism for Malaysian actors.
Fahmi said Finas would work with the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Intellectual Property Corporation of Malaysia.
He said the mechanism could ensure actors continued to receive reasonable economic benefits when works featuring their performances were commercially exploited after their initial release.
He said this included through television reruns, streaming platforms and international markets.
Fahmi said the Copyright Act 1987 currently provided certain rights to performers.
"However, there is currently no specific mechanism for residual payments for audiovisual works.
"Actors' remuneration is generally determined based on the terms and conditions agreed between the actors and producers or rights holders," he said.
Fahmi said the views of stakeholders would also be taken into account, including the Federation of Malaysian Film Industry Workers Associations, actors' associations and producers' associations, to ensure the proposed mechanism considered the interests of all parties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-bank officer fined RM36,000 for bribery, now works as delivery rider
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A former bank officer was fined RM36,000 by the Sessions Court today on six charges of failing to report receiving more than RM80,000 in bribes for personal loan financing.
Judge Rosli Ahmad imposed the sentence on Noor Iskandar Aziz, 45, and ordered him to serve six months' imprisonment if he failed to settle the fine.
According to the alternative charges, Iskandar was accused of receiving six cash deposits, totalling over RM80,000, into accounts belonging to himself and his wife, from two individuals and a company, CSA Infinite Consultancy.
The gratification was for assisting the personal loan financing applications of customers of CSA Academy Sdn Bhd at a bank, concurrently with the personal loan applications of customers at several other financial institutions.
The accused, however, failed to report the gratification to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) or a police officer.
The offences were committed at two banks in Kuala Lumpur and Setia Alam between Oct 5, 2021 and May 11, 2023, under Section 25(1) of the MACC Act 2009 and punishable under Section 25(2) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum fine of RM100,000 or imprisonment for a maximum of 10 years, or both.
Deputy public prosecutor Irna Julieza Maaras urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence to serve the accused and the community a lesson.
Counsel Sean Dudley, appearing for the accused, pleaded for a fine only, on the ground that his client, who works as a delivery rider, supports his wife and two children.
"The accused suffers from hypertension, which requires continuous treatment and medication. He has also extended full cooperation to the MACC throughout the investigation, and has no previous criminal record," he said.

Title: 2027 Budget to focus on growth, easing cost pressures, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The fifth Madani budget will focus on strengthening the economy while ensuring economic growth translates into better quality of life for the people, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said economic growth alone was insufficient if some people continued to face rising living costs.
"Therefore, the 2027 Budget will continue to focus on alleviating burdens, protecting the people, creating opportunities, and ensuring that the benefits of development are felt more equitably," he said in a post on X today.
"I will present all the details this Friday, God willing," he said.
Earlier today, Anwar briefed the media on the 2027 Budget.
He is scheduled to table the budget in the Dewan Rakyat this Friday at 3.30pm.

Title: Toddler undergoes three surgeries after stray dog attack last month
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A two-year-old girl who was attacked by five stray dogs in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, last month has undergone three surgeries and will require several more procedures before she can be discharged from hospital.
Nur Haira Wafiqah is currently warded at the Paediatric Special Surgery Ward of Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA), Johor Baru, where she is under the close supervision of seven specialist doctors, her father said.
Mohammad Hamizi Hamdan, 37, said the first three surgeries involved treating and closing wounds on various parts of his daughter's body and head caused by the animal bites.
"The wounds on my daughter's legs, arms and body have started to heal, but the injuries to her head still require intensive treatment.
"This is Haira's fourth week receiving treatment at HSA and she is scheduled to undergo another surgery on her head this week," he said.
He said this when receiving a visit from a delegation of the Batu Pahat Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) Women's Association (Pelitawanis), at his home today.
Hamizi said the next series of surgeries would focus on tissue treatment, including the removal, repair and transplantation of damaged tissue.
The procedures will be carried out periodically and are expected to require Haira to remain in hospital for several more months.
"My wife, Nur Wahyuni Harun, 36, takes care of Haira at the hospital, while I travel back and forth from Batu Pahat to Johor Baru two to three times a week.
"After the first surgery, which took more than seven hours on the day of the incident, Haira only regained consciousness three days later. At first, she did not recognise anyone, but, Alhamdulillah, a few days later she began recognising me and her mother," he said.
He said Haira is now in stable condition, able to converse and eat normally.
However, doctors had informed the family that she could suffer permanent impairment, including impaired hair growth on several parts of her head.
Meanwhile, Batu Pahat TNB Pelitawanis chairman Datin Adib Nafilah Abu Dardak said the visit was to check on Haira's latest condition and present a contribution to help ease the family's financial burden.
In the 7am incident on Sept 5, Haira sustained serious injuries to almost her entire body after being attacked by a pack of stray dogs in front of her house.
Batu Pahat police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani had earlier confirmed that the victim was rushed to Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) in Batu Pahat for initial treatment before being transferred to HSA for specialist treatment.

Title: Indonesia records 1,201 hotspots as haze persists in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Forest and land fires in Indonesia continued to burn, with 1,201 high-confidence hotspots recorded nationwide today, down by 158 from yesterday.
The Forestry Ministry said Central Kalimantan recorded 182 hotspots, the highest among the six priority provinces, followed by South Sumatra (71), West Kalimantan (34), Jambi (21) and South Kalimantan (18), while Riau recorded none.
"The government has put 61 aerial units on standby, comprising 17 for patrol and weather modification operations and 44 for water bombing, while ground operations, firefighting, firebreaks, as well as the wetting and cooling of peatlands, will continue to prevent fires from reigniting," the ministry said in a social media post.
Thick smoke from the ongoing fires caused transboundary haze to affect neighbouring countries, including Malaysia, where 35 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) levels as of 10 am, prompting schools in Johor to close for two days due to unhealthy air quality.
Meanwhile, Indonesian Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni said the ministry was committed to gradually increasing the country's forest police force from about 4,500 personnel currently to 70,000 within three to four years, as announced by President Prabowo Subianto.
"For us at the Forestry Ministry, strengthening the forest police is very important to improve the monitoring and protection of forest areas, including from the threat of encroachment and forest fires," Raja Juli said in an Instagram post.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian Parliament's Palestine Caucus to submit motion on Gaza genocide for debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Parliament's Palestine Caucus will submit a proposed motion on the genocide in Gaza to the Office of the Dewan Rakyat Speaker and seek to have it scheduled for debate during next week's parliamentary sitting.
Its chairman, Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh, said the proposed motion would include calls for a lasting ceasefire, the protection of civilians, and safe, sustained and unhindered access to humanitarian aid.
"Rejecting the forced displacement of Palestinians and affirming their right to self-determination, while supporting the processes of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and the International Criminal Court (ICC) within their respective jurisdictions, as well as respecting relevant international judicial decisions and orders," he said.
Syed Ibrahim, who is natural resources and environmental sustainability deputy minister, said this at a press conference held in conjunction with the Three-Year Commemoration of the Gaza Genocide at the Parliament building here today.
The Ledang member of parliament also said the motion would call for efforts to strengthen diplomatic action, including scrutiny of military assistance and arms transfers that risk facilitating violations of international law.
"In addition, to establish a coordinated Malaysian framework for the recovery of Gaza, prioritising healthcare, education, child rehabilitation and Palestinian-led reconstruction," he said.
In this regard, Syed Ibrahim said the Caucus called for sufficient time to be allocated to allow for substantive debate and the participation of MPs from across the political divide.
"To ensure the success of this initiative, the Caucus calls for coordinated engagement with the government as well as government and opposition MPs to finalise the motion and facilitate its tabling and scheduling in accordance with the Standing Orders in force," he said.
Meanwhile, he also called on the public to participate in the Three-Year Commemoration of the Gaza Genocide gathering from 2pm to 5pm this Friday, which will begin at Menara Tabung Haji before proceeding to the United States embassy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Unsubsidised RON97 and RON95 up 15 sen, diesel holds at RM5.27
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The retail prices of RON97 and unsubsidised RON95 petrol will rise by 15 sen per litre to RM5.15 and RM4.67 respectively from tomorrow until Oct 14.
Unsubsidised diesel will remain at RM5.27 per litre during the same period.
The Finance Ministry (MoF) said the increase was driven by pressure on the supply of refined petroleum products in the international market, despite the gradual recovery of crude oil flows from West Asia.
"Although crude oil flows from West Asia are gradually recovering, global crude oil prices remain high. Throughout the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period, Brent crude oil prices continued to hover around US$100 per barrel," it said in a statement.
The ministry said price pressures were increasingly concentrated on refined petroleum products following China's suspension of most fuel exports for October, limiting supplies in the international market.
"The recovery of global refining capacity and refined petroleum product supplies remains important in reducing price pressures in the medium term," it said.
The ministry said developments in the conflicts in West Asia and between Russia and Ukraine continued to pose risks to the stability of global petroleum supplies and prices.
"The Madani government will continue to protect the rakyat and businesses from the impact of this global volatility, including by maintaining targeted Budi Madani subsidies for eligible users," it said.
Meanwhile, Budi95 recipients would continue to pay RM1.99 per litre compared to the unsubsidised RON95 price of RM4.67 per litre, with the government bearing a subsidy of RM2.68 per litre, or 57 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
The ministry said fuel supplies in the country remained sufficient but urged consumers to use fuel prudently, plan journeys efficiently and reduce unnecessary travel to help conserve supplies and manage subsidy expenditure.
It added that the Madani government would continue to adopt a prudent approach to cushion the impact of price fluctuations while ensuring the country's fuel supply remained sufficient and secure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ketum stash found during social media livestream
Article:
SUBANG JAYA: Police have confirmed the discovery of a container holding 21 bottles of liquid believed to be ketum juice at Kampung Seri Langkas, Puchong Permai, yesterday.
Subang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said police received a report about the discovery at 8.45pm from a member of the public who live-streaming at the location.
"At 9pm, a team of officers and personnel from the Narcotics Crime Investigation Division of the Subang Jaya district police headquarters and Bukit Puchong police station went to the location to conduct an inspection.
"An inspection of an unnumbered house found a covered plastic container holding 21 plastic bottles containing liquid believed to be ketum juice," he said in a statement today.
He said the liquid, estimated at 10,500 ml (10.5l), was seized by police for further investigation under Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952.
He said further investigations were underway to identify those involved in possessing the prohibited substance.
"Police reiterate their continued commitment to curbing the distribution of prohibited substances and urge the public to continue providing information to assist efforts to combat crime," he said.
Earlier, several viral video clips showed a group of individuals discovering the liquid believed to be ketum juice during a social media livestream about the Rohingya refugee settlement in the area.

Title: Nurse stabbed six times by husband in stable condition
Article:
KOTA BARU: The nurse who was stabbed six times by her husband at their home in Kampung Padang Lepai near Kadok on Monday is now in stable condition.
Her daughter, 19, said her mother regained consciousness yesterday afternoon but remained under close observation at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital (HRPZ II).
"According to the doctors, my mother's condition started to stabilise today, but she still requires close monitoring by the hospital.
"My siblings and other family members take turns staying with her at the hospital," said the student, the eldest of three siblings.
She said her mother had also started speaking, although she remained weak.
The 44-year-old victim, who works as a nurse at Klinik Kesihatan Chempaka, was allegedly
stabbed by her husband
during an incident about 8.40pm on Monday.
She was stabbed in her body and neck, and sustained injuries to her liver and intestines.
The suspect, who is unemployed, surrendered himself at the Nilam Puri police station about 9.15pm the same day.
Police have obtained a seven-day remand order against the 47-year-old suspect.
The case is being investigated under Section 326 of Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means.
Anyone found guilty is liable to up to 20 years' jail, and a fine or whipping.

Title: Salutica eyes RM16.2m placement to fund property expansion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Salutica Bhd has proposed a private placement of up to 30 per cent of its issued shares to raise up to RM16.18 million to fund its expansion into property development and construction.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the placement would involve up to 30 per cent of its issued shares, excluding treasury shares, to third-party investors to be identified later.
Based on an illustrative issue price of 11.5 sen per share, the exercise will raise gross proceeds of up to RM16.18 million.
The final issue price will be fixed later at a discount of not more than 20 per cent to the five-day volume-weighted average market price of Salutica shares immediately before the price-fixing date.
Of the proceeds, RM8 million will be allocated to expanding the proposed property development and construction business, while up to RM8 million will be used to expand its existing manufacturing operations.
Salutica said the proposed diversification would cover property development, construction and related activities.
This includes design-and-build works, trading and supplying construction materials, property management and property investment.
The company currently derives all of its revenue from manufacturing, which has been loss-making in recent financial years.
It recorded a net loss of RM23.75 million for the 12 months ended June 30, 2026, compared with RM29.76 million in the financial year ended June 30, 2025.
Salutica said the diversification would broaden its earnings base and reduce its reliance on manufacturing.
It is initially targeting smaller construction and property-related projects before taking on larger projects as it gains experience.
As at Sept 15, Salutica had not secured or entered into any construction, property development or property investment projects.
The proposed private placement and diversification are subject to shareholders' approval at an extraordinary general meeting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor haze worsens as all monitoring stations record unhealthy API readings
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Haze conditions worsened across Johor tonight, with all eight air quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
As of 8pm, Segamat recorded the highest reading at 179, followed by Pasir Gudang (178), Larkin (175), Batu Pahat and Kluang (169 each), Kota Tinggi and Pengerang (169 each), and Tangkak (168).
The readings came after the state government announced that all schools in Johor would be closed for two days tomorrow and Friday as a precautionary measure.
The closure follows
a decree by Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail,
with Johor Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali saying the move was aimed at protecting pupils' health and safety.
The state government and relevant agencies are continuing to monitor API readings as the haze situation develops.
The worsening haze in Johor comes amid a wider regional haze situation, with neighbouring Indonesia also facing the effects of wildfires.
AFP reported that Indonesia's government has been accused of "gross negligence" in a lawsuit over toxic haze from wildfires that blanketed parts of Borneo.
The lawsuit, filed against President Prabowo Subianto and nine other officials, came as fires and smoke in West Kalimantan forced school closures and sent hundreds of people for treatment for respiratory problems.
The plaintiffs, including the West Kalimantan chapter of Indigenous rights group AMAN,
accused the government
of failing to prevent and tackle recurring forest and land fires.

Title: Pahang cops still hunting prime suspect in Genting jewellery heist
Article:
KUANTAN: Pahang police are still hunting the suspected mastermind behind the RM1.7 million jewellery heist at SkyAvenue, Genting Highlands, following the arrest of seven suspects.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the suspects, including a woman, are believed to be linked to the mastermind.
"The suspects include three foreigners, two men and a woman. They are aged between 25 and 64," he said.
Azry said six suspects, including the woman, had been released on police bail, while the Chinese national arrested at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport yesterday had been remanded until Oct 10.
He said the case was being investigated under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code for armed gang robbery.
Earlier today, Azry told reporters in Bentong that the
Chinese national, in his 40s,
was the latest suspect to be detained after arriving at KLIA yesterday.
In the Aug 17 robbery, three masked men armed with an axe and crowbars
broke into the goldsmith's shop
before fleeing with jewellery worth about RM1.7 million.

Title: Che' Puan Mahkota Johor: Protecting children from sexual exploitation everyone's responsibility
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Protecting children from sexual exploitation is a shared responsibility requiring close inter-agency cooperation, Che' Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Bustamam said today.
The Regent of Johor's consort said children's safety and their best interests must always remain the priority.
"The task of protecting these children must be treated as a shared responsibility, with agencies working closely to ensure vulnerable children are protected and their best interests remain paramount.
"Stronger communication, coordinated action and a clear understanding of each agency's role were crucial in dealing with cases involving the sexual exploitation of children," she said in a royal address.
She was speaking at the the "Multi-Agency Seminar: Strengthening Collaboration in Handling Cases of Sexual Exploitation of Children".
The seminar brought together agencies involved in identifying, protecting, investigating and supporting children affected by sexual exploitation.
It was aimed at strengthening coordination and ensuring cases are handled in a more effective and child-centred manner.
Che' Puan Khaleeda also stressed that children were invaluable and parents had a fundamental role in providing them with love, care and protection.
"Be present in their lives, listen to their voices and ensure that home is always the safest place for them to seek refuge," she said.
Her Highness said protecting children could not rest with a single agency, but required all parties to work together and respond effectively when a child was at risk.
The programme was attended by the Johor menteri besar's wife, Sharmin Fazlina Mohd Shukor; state Women, Family and Community Development Committee chairman Hasrunizah Hassan; state deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Hoo Chuan Huat, as well as representatives from various agencies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: All Johor schools to close for two days starting tomorrow by  Regent’s decree over unhealthy API
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 7 — The Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail has decreed for all schools in the state to close following the persistent haze and unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings,” said Johor Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali.
He explained that the two-day closure, starting tomorrow and the following day, was due to the ongoing haze compounded with a deteriorating air quality across all districts in the state.
“The closure affects 617,258 students across 1,198 schools that comes under the administration of the Education Ministry.
"All schools throughout Johor will be closed on October 8 and 9 as a precautionary measure to safeguard the student’s safety and health,” he said in a statement issued today.
Dr Muhammad Naqib pointed out that for schools involved in the Year 4 Learning Matrix (MPT4) or any other assessments, the implementation will be postponed and rescheduled.
He said this will be subjected to directives from the Johor Education Department (JPNJ) and relevant authorities.
“During the two-day closure period, Teaching and Learning at Home (PdPR) sessions will be conducted to ensure the learning process continues,” he said, adding that the state government and relevant agencies will continue to monitor API readings regularly.
Dr Muhammad Naqib said the state government understands that such a decision may impact parents and guardians who still need to work.
Therefore, he said the granting of appropriate work flexibility to affected parents or guardians by their employers will be greatly appreciated.
“I also urge parents to continue monitoring their children's health, ensure they stay hydrated and limit any outdoor activities.
“Parents or guardians need to seek immediate medical attention if their children experience coughing, sore throat or shortness of breath," he said.
Earlier, Johor recorded unhealthy API readings, with figures between 161 and 197, from eight monitoring stations.
Batu Pahat was the worst hit with an API reading of 197 in the morning.
Yesterday a total of 335 education institutions in the Batu Pahat district were ordered to close after the API reading in the district reached 208 last night.

Title: Laos meth bust: Four arrested in Subang Airport hangar raid over 521kg found in Learjet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) today raided a hangar at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang, believed to be linked to the seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs in Laos last week.
Port Klang AKPS Commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said the special operation was conducted jointly with the Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (JSJN), AKPS, Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters (IPD), Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad Auxiliary Police (AVSEC) and Special Branch Travel Control Officers (TCO).
“I can confirm that there was a raid and arrests. The operation was conducted jointly... we had been planning it since yesterday, and the operation began at noon today and has since been completed,” he told Bernama when contacted today.
Four individuals were reportedly arrested while preparing for a flight and were handed over to the Bukit Aman JSJN for further investigation.
However, Nik Ezanee declined to disclose details of the operation or the identities of the suspects, leaving it to the Bukit Aman JSJN to provide further information on the arrests.
On October 1, Laos police seized 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from a private Learjet that had arrived from Subang.
Following the seizure, 13 individuals, including a Malaysian, Singaporean and Filipino, were detained by the Laotian authorities to assist investigations into the cross-border drug trafficking case. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Budget 2027 to turn economic growth into better lives for Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Fifth Madani Budget is based on a clear resolve to strengthen the nation’s economy and translate growth into a better life for the people.
Anwar said he is aware that economic growth alone is insufficient if some citizens still face rising living costs.
Therefore, he said that Budget 2027 will continue to focus on alleviating burdens, protecting the people, creating opportunities, and ensuring that the benefits of development are felt more equitably.
“I will present all details this Friday, Insya-Allah,” he said in a post on X today.
Earlier today, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, briefed the media on the Madani 2027 Budget to explain the Madani government’s direction and efforts for the people.
The prime minister will present the Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat this Friday at 3.30pm. — Bernama

Title: Johor MB pushes for Asean emergency talks as haze hits unhealthy levels
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 7 — Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi called on the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) to play a more active role and to convene an emergency meeting to address the haze crisis.
He said the current transboundary haze situation is affecting Johor, particularly in the areas of public health and a deteriorating air quality in several areas of the state.
“Asean nations possessing the expertise, assets, and capabilities can step forward to assist based on needs, through coordination and mutual agreement.
“With effective cooperation, prevention, monitoring and response, efforts can be implemented immediately and effectively for the people across the region,” he said in a statement issued today.
Onn Hafiz hopes the proposal will be considered by Asean’s leadership to restore the situation and ensure the public can return to living in a safer and healthier environment.
He added that the proposal was raised during an earlier meeting with the Indonesian consul general in Johor Bahru Sigit Suryantoro Widiyanto.
“I conveyed the state government’s concerns and expressed hope that efforts to tackle the root causes of the haze can be further intensified.
“Our approach here is not to point fingers at any party, but rather to find a collective solution. The impact transcends our national borders,” he said.
Onn Hafiz explained that when air pollution crosses borders and affects neighboring countries, including Malaysia, the issue inevitably requires closer regional cooperation for mutual benefit.
Earlier today, Johor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with figures between 161 and 197, in eight monitoring stations.
Batu Pahat was the worst hit with an API reading of 197 in the morning.
Yesterday a total of 335 education institutions in the Batu Pahat district were ordered to close today after the API reading in the district reached 208 last night.

Title: Former N. Sembilan exco members barred only from exco rooms but can still enter Wisma Negeri, says A-G
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The 10 state assemblymen who previously served as Negeri Sembilan executive councillors (exco) are only barred from entering their exco rooms following their dismissal from the posts on September 24, which means they are no longer members of the state administration.
However, they may still enter state government buildings in their capacity as elected representatives and carry out their duties as assemblymen, particularly to attend to matters involving their constituents.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said the ban also meant the former exco members were not allowed to enter their respective rooms, including to collect personal belongings left at the offices.
“As elected representatives, they can come to Wisma Negeri as usual to attend to official matters, but access to the exco rooms is not allowed because they are no longer members of the state administration,” he said when contacted today.
The media reported today that the 10 assemblymen — Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah — who are challenging the cancellation of their appointments as state exco members, have applied to the Seremban High Court to declare their dismissals null and void, invalid and of no effect.
All the plaintiffs filed originating summonses at the Seremban High Court through Messrs Hafarizam Wan & Aisha Mubarak last Monday against the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary and the Negeri Sembilan state government as defendants.
On whether any decisions had been made by the 10 former exco members before their dismissal, Mohd Dusuki said such decisions were valid and remained in force as they were still holding exco positions at the time.
“Decisions made while they were still exco members are valid. After their dismissal, they no longer have the authority to make decisions as exco members,” he said.

Title: Perak Perhilitan: Malayan tigers will only be captured if they threaten public safety
Article:
IPOH, Oct 7 — The Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) will only capture or translocate Malayan tigers if an assessment finds that their presence poses a threat to public safety.
Perak Perhilitan director Dr Pazil Abdul Patah said the assessment takes into account the tiger’s behaviour, frequency and duration of sightings, distance from residential areas, movement patterns, and evidence of interactions or attacks involving humans or livestock.
“If the assessment shows a clear and continuing threat to human safety, Perhilitan will take appropriate action based on technical assessments in the field,” he told Bernama.
Five tiger sightings or incidents have been recorded in Perak from January to October this year, beginning with a report of a roar in Proton City, Tanjung Malim on January 10, followed by an image captured in Bukit Bangkong, Chemor on July 14 and the capture of a tigress in Hulu Kinta on July 22.
This was followed by a fatal attack in Pos Perwor, Sungai Siput on September 21 and the discovery of tiger footprints at Kem Sultan Nazrin Shah, 69 Komando, Ulu Kinta on September 29.
Pazil said tiger sightings near human settlements did not necessarily mean that their forest habitat or roaming areas were shrinking, as movements could also be influenced by prey availability, habitat conditions, human disturbance, development and land use, as well as the animals’ natural movements.
“In some situations, tigers may move through forest edges or ecological corridors within their home range and be detected near human settlements by chance,” he said.
He said Perhilitan continuously monitored prey species such as barking deer, deer and wild boar in the state’s main forest reserves, with camera traps, field surveys and population data used to assess prey availability.
Pazil said complaints about tiger sightings were assessed based on the location, time, physical evidence and current situation to determine the priority and appropriate deployment of personnel, with control teams sent to the field when there was a risk to public safety.
He said besides physical measures such as setting traps, Perhilitan also provided technical advice and safety guidance, including advising residents in high-risk areas to avoid going out alone in the early morning or late evening, refrain from provoking tigers and leave the handling of such cases to the department. — Bernama
